Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with a smooth contour and preserved diaphragmatic shape, which is characteristic of upward displacement by an enlarged liver (hepatomegaly) rather than eventration or paralysis. There is no evidence of subdiaphragmatic air (abscess), bilateral effusions, or scalloping/retrocardiac mass suggestive of lymphangioma or hiatal hernia.
